summary: Mille Fiori is a solitaire-ish Knizia pattern-building game about placing glass tiles across five interconnected boards while occasionally jostling for majority spots. Turns are quick and the puzzle is mostly about efficient personal engine-building rather than fighting opponents.
praised: quick individual turns despite a meaty ruleset
criticised: fiddly to teach with many icons/boards
interaction feels thin for a Knizia design
can feel like solitaire with occasional bumps

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with occasional area majority
interaction.detail: Each player mostly develops their own board and card tableau independently, with limited direct interaction through shared majority spaces on the board rather than direct conflict.

subsystems: tableau/pattern building across production stages (workshops, houses, people)
scoring.how_you_win: You place action pawns and tiles to build out glass-production chains and ship goods through the harbor; when the triggering track/tile supply is exhausted, points from completed patterns and shipping majorities are totaled and the highest sum wins.
